title: routing-policy-eval-entropy-caused-incompatible-variant-fallback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Post-incident ticket documenting the February 11 routing/fallback incident where nondeterministic policy evaluation led to selection of an incompatible model variant and a cross-region retry loop. This ticket captures timeline, root cause, mitigations applied, and tracked action items for preventing recurrence.
impact: Between 07:12-07:45 UTC on 2026-02-11 several customer services using Dedicated pools and hosted fallbacks experienced elevated 5xx rates and tail latency. Approximately 2.8k requests were retried across regions; 15% of routed requests observed model-incompatibility failures (invalid kv-cache shape) causing request aborts and cascading retries that increased load on neighboring regions. Customer-facing errors mostly returned 502/ERR_MODEL_MISMATCH. Several enterprise customers reported degraded SLAs and opened support incidents.
root_cause: Policy evaluation order relied on an unordered map iteration in our Go routing service. When multiple candidate routes scored equally under the policy rules (cost/latency/availability), the implicit map iteration tie-breaker produced nondeterministic ordering. This allowed a fallback path to pick an incompatible model variant (legacy-quantized family) for a request expecting an unquantized variant, triggering KV-cache deserialization errors. Additionally, the retryer logic did not verify variant compatibility before re-enqueueing on a remote region, which combined with stale capacity cache entries created a cross-region reroute loop under transient capacity pressure.
timeline: 2026-02-11 07:12 UTC - Spike in errors and increased latency alerted by per-route SLO dashboards (Grafana: /d/runtime-routing/route-errors)
2026-02-11 07:18 UTC - Initial investigation by on-call routing engineer (Marcus Li) identified model-mismatch errors in request logs and KV-cache stack traces

2026-02-11 07:25 UTC - Emergency mitigation: temporarily disabled cross-region retries for affected customer tiers and applied stricter compatibility checks in the gateway (hotfix deployed runtime-1.22-hotfix.1)
2026-02-11 07:33 UTC - Errors decreased after mitigation but tail latency remained elevated due to increased cold-starts on local pools
2026-02-11 09:00 UTC - Post-incident triage started; assigned follow-ups and owners
2026-02-12 - Root cause analysis completed and initial PR prepared to enforce deterministic policy ordering and compatibility guardrails (PR 3821)
2026-02-18 - Additional tests added to routing e2e suite to simulate equal-score candidates and capacity flapping
2026-03-02 - Canary rollout of deterministic policy sort and retry compatibility checks to 10% of traffic; monitoring OK
2026-03-09 - Full rollout to production completed with telemetry and dashboards updated
mitigations: Hotfix: disable cross-region automatic retries for affected tiers and reduce retry window (runtime-1.22-hotfix.1)
Gate: add explicit variant-compatibility check in retryer to reject enqueues that would pick a different model family
Patch: enforce deterministic ordering in policy evaluation by sorting candidate routes by explicit sort key rather than relying on map iteration
Telemetry: add per-request policy decision logs and tag chosen-variant metadata to traces
Observability: new Grafana panel showing ‘tie-break’ occurrences and fallback-to-incompatible-variant counts
action_items: AI-1: Merge PR to enforce deterministic policy ordering and backfill unit tests (owner: Marcus Li, estimate: 3) - target: 2026-02-20

AI-2: Add compatibility validation in the retryer and in the routing decision path to prevent selecting variants with incompatible KV/cache shapes (owner: Priya Menon, estimate: 5) - target: 2026-02-25
AI-3: Create synthetic canary that simulates equal-score candidate scenarios and capacity flapping to catch tie-break regressions (owner: SRE team, estimate: 8) - target: 2026-03-01
AI-4: Update runbook/playbook with a checklist for variant compatibility checks and emergency knobs for cross-region retries (owner: Jordan Kim, estimate: 2) - target: 2026-02-22

AI-5: Add telemetry retention for per-route decision traces (30 days) and instrument alert when >0.1% of requests hit an incompatible-variant fallback (owner: Observability, estimate: 3) - target: 2026-03-05
AI-6: Post-deploy verification and load test to validate behavior under burst capacity conditions and ensure no retry-loop occurs (owner: Performance team, estimate: 5) - target: 2026-03-10
